## `slot`

Run builds on one shared pool of build slots.

`slot <command…>` sends the command to the slot daemon, which queues it until enough slots are free, runs it, streams its output back and exits with its code. Every build that goes through the daemon shares one GNU-make jobserver, so cargo, rustc and make draw parallelism from the same pool and the machine is never oversubscribed.

```text
slot [OPTIONS]
       slot <COMMAND>
```

- `--local`: Run the command here, without the daemon (default `false`)

### `slot serve`

Run the daemon: the slot pool, the job queue and the web UI

```text
slot serve [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: Unix socket clients connect to (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)
- `--http`: Web UI address; `off` disables it (default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--tokens`: Build slots in the pool (jobserver tokens); default: the number of CPUs
- `--go-tokens`: Slots a go job holds; go's -p is set to match (default `4`)
- `--state-dir`: Jobserver FIFO and job log
- `--ws-root`: Where remote clients sync workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/ws`)
- `--cache-root`: Target dirs and caches for synced workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/cache`)
- `--memory-max`: systemd `MemoryMax` per job, for example 24G
- `--keep-jobs`: Finished jobs kept in memory and shown in the UI (default `500`)
- `--cpu-weight`: systemd `CPUWeight` for every job (interactive apps default to 100); 0 leaves it unset. Applied to the daemon's own unit at start (default `20`)

### `slot proxy`

Bridge stdin/stdout to the daemon's socket (remote clients run this over ssh)

```text
slot proxy [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: The daemon's socket (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)

### `slot run`

Run a build command; use this when the command's name is also a slot subcommand

```text
slot run [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...
```

- `<COMMAND>`: The command and its arguments
